summary: Unit tests (license-checker.bats) are well-organized with good cycle-based structure and comprehensive coverage of core functionality: manifest parsing (JSON, requirements.txt), license classification, policy loading, mocking, exit codes, and output formats. However, workflow integration tests (workflow.bats) depend on missing files (tests/check_workflow.py validator, tests/cases/*/fixtures) and cannot run without them. This breaks a critical testing layer. Additionally, rigor gaps: no tests for unreadable files (permissions), malformed policy files (missing =, empty files), special characters in package names, or policy file format edge cases. The test suite is partially functional but incomplete—unit tests alone would pass, but the required end-to-end act/workflow testing cannot execute without the missing fixture directories and Python validator.
